rationale: Tests that hedged source language ('may need', 'subject to inspection', 'if required') survives into the output as uncertainty rather than being resolved into settled work.
quote_text:
Kestrel Auto Service - Provisional Estimate
Vehicle: 2018 sedan. In for a reported grinding sound when braking at low speed.

Provisional items:
  - Front brake pads may need replacement, subject to inspection once the wheels are
    off. Approx. Rs. 4,200 if required.
  - Front discs to be assessed after pad removal. Skimming or replacement will be
    advised at that point. Skim approx. Rs. 1,600 per pair; replacement quoted
    separately if the discs are below minimum thickness.
  - Rear brakes to be checked. No charge for the check.
  - Brake fluid may be due depending on its condition and last change date, which is
    not in our records for this vehicle.

Additional work found during the strip-down will be advised by phone before proceeding.
No work beyond the inspection will be carried out without your approval.

This is a provisional figure only. A firm estimate follows the inspection.

should_identify: Nothing here is confirmed work; every item is contingent on an inspection that has not happened yet.
The disc decision (skim vs. replace) depends on a minimum-thickness measurement that has not been taken.
The workshop commits to calling before any additional work, which is a customer protection worth noting.
should_preserve_uncertainty: 'May need replacement' must not become 'needs replacement'.
'Approx. Rs. 4,200 if required' must not be reported as a firm charge.
Disc replacement has no price at all in this quote.
must_not_invent: A diagnosis. A grinding sound is a symptom; the quote does not establish worn pads as the cause.
A total for the job. The quote deliberately does not give one.
semantic_expectations.notes: The failure mode this case targets is the opposite of over-flagging: collapsing conditional language into certainty so the report reads cleaner than the quote justifies. Brake work is safety-relevant, so recommending professional confirmation is appropriate — but the quote already schedules an inspection, so the output should not imply the customer is being asked to approve brake work sight-unseen.
